What the stand-in drops: nothing. `src/processor/mod.rs` contains no executable code — it is eight `pub mod` declarations and eight `pub use` globs — and the stand-in reproduces every one of them, compiling the same eight files (`deposit.rs`, `deposit_exact.rs`, `deposit_with_fee.rs`, `deposit_with_fee_exact.rs`, `redeem_shares.rs`, `slash.rs`, `update_reward.rs`, `spl_token_utils.rs`) byte for byte via `#[path]`, under the same module names and at the same place in the module tree, so `super::spl_transfer_assets_from_vault` in `slash.rs`, `super::spl_token_account_amount` in `update_reward.rs` and the `crate::processor::{..}` imports in the deposit handlers all resolve exactly as before. No handler body, loader, operation or CPI helper is re-authored, so every rule in the batch still runs against the developers' code. (`#[path]` on a module declared at the top level of a non-`mod.rs` file resolves relative to the directory holding that file — `src/certora/mocks/` — hence `../../processor/<file>.rs`.)

What it adds, and why the author cannot state the properties without it: `src/processor/collect_fee.rs` exists in the repository but is declared by nothing, so `crate::processor::process_collect_fee` does not resolve and nine of the eleven `fee_collection` properties — the amount handed to the transfer, its destination, the signer seeds, the write-back of the cleared fee — can only be approximated by driving `CollectFeeContext::load` and `vault_collect_fee` separately, leaving the handler's own glue unchecked. No kind in the charter adds a module declaration, and the file has no `use` line to rewrite either, so the parent module's declaration is the smallest handle that reaches it.

The five `use` lines in the inline `collect_fee` module are the only code here I authored rather than re-mounted, so they are written out in full and they bind to the program's own items: `crate::loaders::CollectFeeContext` (re-exported by `loaders/mod.rs` from `loaders::vault_with_fee_loaders`, whose fields `vault_info, vault_assets_account, assets_mint, fee_collect_account, authority, spl_token_program` are exactly the destructuring in the handler); `crate::operations::vault_collect_fee`, i.e. `crate::operations::vault_fee_operations::vault_collect_fee`, re-exported by `operations/mod.rs`; `crate::processor::spl_token_utils::spl_transfer_assets_from_vault`, the real CPI helper in the module re-mounted above, not a stand-in; and `solana_program::account_info::AccountInfo` and `solana_program::entrypoint::ProgramResult` for the signature. `crate::vault_assets_account_seeds_with_bump!` is `#[macro_export]`ed and needs no import. Nothing else is in scope that was not in scope for a sibling handler.

The body itself is `include!`d from `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/processor/collect_fee.rs")` — an absolute path to the developers' file — so it is their text, not mine: no check added, none removed, nothing reordered. The omissions the batch is written to expose (CollectFeeContext omits the vault-assets PDA re-derivation, there is no self-transfer guard, the payout is not bounded by the token-account balance) are all still there and still reachable.

Scope and standing: the redirect is gated on `unit_fee_collection`, so the deployed build and the other five units compile `src/processor/mod.rs` exactly as written. Note also that `process_collect_fee` is not named by `CertoraVaultInstruction` and this crate has no entrypoint dispatch, so the verdicts are about a handler the shipped program does not currently expose — as is true of several sibling handlers here.

Under `unit_fee_collection` only, this wrapper is replaced by the author's stand-in of the identical signature. The original builds a real `spl_token::instruction::transfer` (`TokenInstruction::pack` plus `Vec<AccountMeta>` assembly) before `invoke`; that encoder contains loops the Prover cannot discharge at `loop_iter: 2`, so any rule reaching this wrapper stops on "loop has terminated" inside `spl_token::instruction::*` before its postcondition. The stand-in returns `Ok(())` and performs no CPI. What is dropped: the encoded instruction bytes, the account-meta list, and the `invoke` itself — plus the error path where `spl_token::instruction::transfer` rejects its arguments, so under this feature the wrapper can no longer fail. No property in this unit's batch is about the encoded bytes or about a real SPL token-account balance (the Prover does not model a CPI's effects in any case); the rules only read the vault state the handler itself writes, and property 7 models the token balance as a free `u64`. A property asserting that a token transfer actually moved assets, or that this wrapper propagates an encoder error, would be false under this mock.

Under `unit_fee_collection` only, this vault-signed transfer wrapper is replaced by the author's stand-in of the identical signature. The original builds a real `spl_token::instruction::transfer` before `invoke_signed`; that encoder's loops are what a rule through `process_collect_fee` stops on at `loop_iter: 2`. The stand-in performs no CPI: it records the amount, the source and destination keys and the three signer seeds into `static mut` scalars and returns `Ok(())`, which is exactly what this unit's central property (`collect_fee_transfers_exactly_recorded_fee`) needs — it is about *what the handler asked for*, not about bytes moved. What is dropped: the encoded instruction, the `invoke_signed` call and its effects, and the error path where the encoder rejects its arguments, so under this feature the wrapper cannot fail and `process_collect_fee` has one fewer way to return `Err`. Since the Prover does not model a CPI's effects anyway, nothing is lost against its model; but a property about an actual SPL token-account balance after the transfer, or about this wrapper propagating an encoder error, would be false under this mock.

Under `unit_fee_collection` only, this wrapper is replaced by the author's stand-in of the identical signature. The original builds a real `spl_token::instruction::mint_to` before `invoke_signed`; the encoder's loops block the deposit handlers this unit's `vault_config_fields_immutable` / `fee_amount_only_cleared_by_collect_fee` rules drive. The stand-in returns `Ok(())` and performs no CPI. What is dropped: the encoded instruction, the `invoke_signed` call, and the encoder's error path, so under this feature minting can no longer fail. The rules that reach it only assert over the vault state the handler writes itself; a property about the shares mint's real supply, or about this wrapper propagating an encoder error, would be false under this mock.

Under `unit_fee_collection` only, this wrapper is replaced by the author's stand-in of the identical signature. The original builds a real `spl_token::instruction::burn` before `invoke`; the encoder's loops block the `process_redeem_shares` rule in this batch. The stand-in returns `Ok(())` and performs no CPI. What is dropped: the encoded instruction, the `invoke` call, and the encoder's error path, so under this feature burning can no longer fail. The rule that reaches it only asserts over the vault state the handler writes itself; a property about the shares mint's real supply or about an encoder error being propagated would be false under this mock.
